disclaimer: This report is for educational and wellness purposes only. It is not a medical diagnosis and does not replace advice from a qualified healthcare professional. HbA1c results should be confirmed by your doctor. Do not start, stop or change any medication without medical advice.

status.label: In the normal range
status.explanation: Your HbA1c reflects average blood glucose over roughly the last 2–3 months and is below the 5.7% threshold used for prediabetes.

summary: Your HbA1c of 5.6% is in the normal range. This report suggests practical food, activity and monitoring steps you can discuss with your doctor.

foods_to_eat: whole grains such as oats, millets and brown rice
nuts and seeds in small amounts
foods_to_avoid: white bread and large portions of white rice
plan.portion_guidance: Use the plate method: fill half your plate with non-starchy vegetables, a quarter with protein and a quarter with whole grains or other starchy foods. Use a 9-inch (23 cm) plate.
plan.hydration: Drink water through the day — about 8 glasses for most adults unless your doctor has advised a fluid limit. Avoid sugary drinks, sweetened tea and coffee, and fruit juice.

exercise: Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate activity a week, such as brisk walking, spread over at least 3 days.
Add muscle-strengthening activity, such as bodyweight exercises, on 2 days a week.
lifestyle.walking_goal: Build up to a 30-minute brisk walk on 5 days a week; a short walk after meals also helps blood glucose.
lifestyle.weight_management: Your weight is not above the healthy range; focus on staying active and eating well.
lifestyle.sleep: Aim for 7–9 hours of sleep with regular sleep and wake times.
stress: Try 5 minutes of slow breathing once or twice a day.
Take short breaks and spend time outdoors or with people you enjoy.
behaviour_change: specific goal each week and track it.
Plan meals and keep healthy snacks within easy reach.

monitoring.name: HbA1c
monitoring.why: Regular screening finds changes before symptoms appear.
monitoring.frequency: Every 3 years, or yearly if your doctor advises because of risk factors

monitoring.name: Blood pressure
monitoring.why: High blood pressure multiplies the heart and kidney risks of high blood glucose.
monitoring.frequency: At every doctor visit; at home regularly if you have high blood pressure

preventive_actions: Keep up regular physical activity and limit time spent sitting.
Choose whole, minimally processed foods and avoid sugary drinks.
Keep your recommended check-ups and tests on schedule.

hba1c_caveat: HbA1c can be less accurate if you have anaemia, kidney disease, a recent blood transfusion or certain haemoglobin variants.
